newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX soars to 4th successive high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX soars to 4th successive high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange for once bucked the trend of international markets as the BUX index reached its fourth successive record high on Wednesday while foreign bourses mostly fell, traders said.
"While the Hungarian market is generally dependent on foreign markets, as an emerging market it still has some independence," said Balazs Bathory of Creditansalt Securities.
The BUX index ended at 3,716.42 points, up 24.36. BUX index futures advanced by between 20.00 and 29.00 points for the fourth nearest maturities and remained steady for the two longest contracts.
The spot BUX advanced but traders saw a mixed picture with 17 papers, including coupons advancing, nine declining and six remaining steady at the close.
Traders believed the recent steady rise will soon stop and the market will go through a corrective phase.
"The index is advancing but after a few more days of rises we can expect a minor correction on the market," Bathory said. "From a technical point of view it's time for that," he said.
The two big pharmaceuticals makers, Richter and Egis both moved upwards.
Richter firmed 20 forints to close at 8,540 forints, below the day's peak of 8,560. Egis rose to 9,900 forints before retreating to end at 9,875, up 25.
Chemicals company Borsodchem remained in focus and rose to close at 3,150 forints, up 50.
Oil firm MOL rose 25 forints to end at 1,775 after news of new oil discoveries from its concessions in Tunisia.
